Package neqsim.process.equipment.util

Class Recycle

java.lang.Object
neqsim.util.NamedBaseClass
neqsim.process.SimulationBaseClass
neqsim.process.equipment.ProcessEquipmentBaseClass
neqsim.process.equipment.util.Recycle
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Runnable, TransientStateParticipant<Recycle.TransientState>, MixerInterface, ProcessEquipmentInterface, ProcessElementInterface, SimulationInterface, NamedInterface
public class Recycle extends ProcessEquipmentBaseClass implements MixerInterface, TransientStateParticipant<Recycle.TransientState>
Recycle class for handling tear streams in process simulations.

This class implements convergence acceleration methods for recycle calculations, including direct substitution, Wegstein acceleration, and Broyden's method.

    • resetIterations

      public void resetIterations()
      resetIterations.

      Called at the start of every process pass. The adaptive-acceleration bookkeeping deliberately survives it: a tear stream that closes across process areas is updated only once per outer pass, so a stall counter that reset here could never reach its threshold and the loop would stay on direct substitution forever. Use resetAdaptiveAcceleration() for a genuine fresh start.

      Deactivates this recycle because its loop flow has collapsed below the configured getMinimumFlow() cutoff.

      A recycle below the cutoff carries no physically meaningful inventory, so it is marked inactive and its four residuals are reported as exactly zero. The previous-iteration snapshot is refreshed at the same time; without that refresh the flow, temperature and pressure balance checks would keep comparing the (negligible) current stream against a stale pre-collapse snapshot, so the recycle would report solved() == false forever. That in turn makes the owning ProcessSystem report NOT SOLVED and spend its whole iteration budget on a dead leg.

      Parameters:
      inletSystem - clone of the (negligible) inlet thermodynamic system to publish on the outlet
      id - current calculation identifier; null leaves existing recycle and outlet identifiers unchanged

    • flowBalanceCheck

      public double flowBalanceCheck()
      Flow residual between this iteration and the previous one.

      The returned value is not dimensionally uniform. Below 1 kg/sec it is the ABSOLUTE change in kg/sec; at or above 1 kg/sec it is the RELATIVE change in PERCENT. A setFlowTolerance(double) of 0.1 therefore means "0.1 kg/sec" on a small loop but "0.1 %" on a large one, and the meaning flips discontinuously across the 1 kg/sec threshold. A returned value of exactly 100 means the loop carried no flow on the previous iteration (a recycle that collapsed and re-opened), not "100 kg/sec".

      This behaviour is retained for backward compatibility. Use getAbsoluteFlowChange() for a properly dimensioned residual (kg/hr) and setAbsoluteFlowTolerance(double) for a scale-independent convergence criterion.

      Returns:
      the flow residual, in kg/sec below 1 kg/sec and in percent at or above 1 kg/sec

    • setAdaptiveAcceleration

      public void setAdaptiveAcceleration(boolean adaptiveAcceleration)
      Enables or disables adaptive acceleration explicitly.

      Direct substitution is robust but converges slowly, and a low-flow loop can oscillate instead of settling, forcing the surrounding process to iterate to its budget. When enabled, a loop whose flow error stops shrinking for 3 consecutive passes switches itself to AccelerationMethod.WEGSTEIN, which damps the oscillation and converges to the same solution. Calling setAccelerationMethod(AccelerationMethod) pins the method and disables the upgrade.

      Adaptive acceleration is disabled for an ordinary legacy ProcessSystem.run(). Automatic convergence tuning may enable it for runUntilConverged(...) unless the caller has made an explicit choice here.

      Parameters:
      adaptiveAcceleration - true to let a stalling loop accelerate itself

      private void updateAdaptiveAcceleration()
      Upgrades a stalling direct-substitution loop to Wegstein acceleration.

      Called once per pass after the errors have been evaluated. A pass counts as stalling when the flow error is still above 0.7 of the previous one - i.e. the loop is oscillating or crawling rather than contracting.

    • applyWegsteinAcceleration

      private double[] applyWegsteinAcceleration(double[] currentInput, double[] currentOutput)
      Applies Wegstein acceleration to calculate accelerated values.

      The Wegstein method uses the formula: x_{n+1} = q * g(x_n) + (1-q) * x_n where q = s / (s - 1) and s is the slope estimate.

      The q-factor is bounded to prevent divergence: - q between qMin and qMax (typically -5 to 0) - q = 0 corresponds to direct substitution - Negative q provides acceleration for monotonic convergence

      Parameters:
      currentInput - the input values for current iteration (x_n)
      currentOutput - the output values from current iteration (g(x_n))
      Returns:
      accelerated values for next iteration input

    • solved

      public boolean solved()
      Returns whether or not the module has been solved.

      A recycle that has been deactivated by the low-flow cutoff (see setMinimumFlow(double)) is reported as solved: it carries no meaningful inventory, so there is nothing left to converge and holding the flowsheet open for it would only burn the iteration budget on a dead leg. A recycle that the user locked inactive is likewise treated as solved, because it never executes.

      The flow criterion is satisfied when EITHER the getErrorFlow() residual is below getFlowTolerance() OR the absolute loop-flow change is below getAbsoluteFlowTolerance() (kg/hr). The absolute term is disabled by default; enabling it gives a scale-independent criterion, which matters because flowBalanceCheck() is an absolute kg/sec residual on small loops and a percentage on large ones.

      Specified by:
      solved in interface SimulationInterface
      Overrides:
      solved in class ProcessEquipmentBaseClass
      Returns:
      a boolean

    • getAbsoluteFlowChange

      public double getAbsoluteFlowChange()
      Absolute change in loop mass flow between the last two iterations.

      Unlike getErrorFlow(), which is an absolute kg/sec residual on loops below 1 kg/sec and a percentage above it, this is always a mass flow and can therefore be compared against a physically meaningful limit.

      Returns:
      the absolute loop-flow change in kg/hr, or NaN before the first balance check

    • getAbsoluteFlowTolerance

      public double getAbsoluteFlowTolerance()
      Absolute flow tolerance used by the recycle convergence check.
      Returns:
      the absolute flow tolerance in kg/hr (0.0 means the criterion is disabled)

    • setAbsoluteFlowTolerance

      public void setAbsoluteFlowTolerance(double absoluteFlowTolerance)
      Sets an absolute flow tolerance for the recycle convergence check.

      The recycle counts as flow-converged when EITHER getErrorFlow() is below getFlowTolerance() OR the absolute loop-flow change is below this value. This is the standard industrial form of the criterion and is the recommended way to get a scale-independent tolerance, because flowBalanceCheck() switches between an absolute kg/sec residual and a percentage at 1 kg/sec. It mirrors ProcessModel.setAbsoluteFlowTolerance(double) at the recycle level.

      Parameters:
      absoluteFlowTolerance - the absolute flow tolerance in kg/hr; must be finite and non-negative. Use 0.0 to disable the criterion (the default)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the value is negative or not finite

    • applyAutoAbsoluteFlowTolerance

      public boolean applyAutoAbsoluteFlowTolerance(double absoluteFlowTolerance)
      Applies an automatically derived absolute flow tolerance, unless the caller already set one.

      Used by the process-level auto-tuner so a tear stream is judged on the same flow noise floor as the plant-wide convergence gate. Without it a recycle keeps iterating on a residual the surrounding model already accepts, or - worse - reports itself solved on a looser criterion than the plant demands.

      Parameters:
      absoluteFlowTolerance - the absolute flow tolerance in kg/hr; must be finite and non-negative
      Returns:
      true if the value was applied, false if an explicit tolerance is already in force
